Apple of the Eye
AP-ul uv thee EYE
noun phrase
Old English æppel for the pupil; idiom for that which is guarded as most precious and sensitive.

📖 Biblical Definition

The apple of the eye is the pupil, the tender center of sight, and by idiom the object of most careful protection. The LORD kept Israel as the apple of his eye in the howling wilderness. David prays, Keep me as the apple of the eye, hide me under the shadow of thy wings. Zechariah warns the nations that he that toucheth you toucheth the apple of his eye. The phrase is covenant affection in bodily image. God’s people are not His casual interest; they are His sensitive possession, and to strike them is to poke the pupil of His regard. The idiom also teaches prayer: the saint asks to be kept with that same jealous care. It does not mean Israel or the church is sinless. It means God’s commitment to His own is intense, protective, and dangerous to their persecutors. Modern speech keeps the idiom for favorites and pets. Scripture keeps it for the LORD’s electing love and guardian zeal. To be the apple of His eye is humbling comfort, not a license for pride, and it calls the nations to fear before they touch what God has sealed as His own.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

The pupil of the eye; idiom for what God guards with most jealous care, applied to His people.

expand to see more

APPLE OF THE EYE, the pupil; that which is most tenderly kept.

God kept Israel as the apple of His eye.

David prays to be kept as the apple of the eye.

To touch God’s people is to touch the apple of His eye.

The idiom means jealous protection, not flattery of the flesh.

📖 Key Scripture

Deu 32:10 — "He found him in a desert land, and in the waste howling wilderness; he led him about, he instructed him, he kept him as the apple of his eye."

Psa 17:8 — "Keep me as the apple of the eye, hide me under the shadow of thy wings,"

Zec 2:8 — "For thus saith the LORD of hosts; After the glory hath he sent me unto the nations which spoiled you: for he that toucheth you toucheth the apple of his eye."

Pro 7:2 — "Keep my commandments, and live; and my law as the apple of thine eye."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

The idiom is sentimentalized into self-esteem slogans; Scripture uses it for God’s protective zeal over His covenant people.

expand to see more

The corruption is to make apple of His eye a pep talk about personal specialness without holiness, church, or Christ. Another is to deny that God has a people He so guards, dissolving election into general warmth for humanity. Zechariah’s warning to the nations makes no sense if the phrase is only private self-talk. God’s eye has an apple, and the nations that poke it will answer.

A soft churchly corruption is ethnic pride without the Messiah, or churchly pride without the cross. The people kept as the apple of His eye are kept for His name and by His blood, not for their boast.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

Apple of the eye means the tender pupil and, by idiom, the people God guards with jealous care.

English idiom — pupil as apple of the eye.

Deuteronomy — kept Israel as the apple of His eye.

Psalms — prayer to be so kept.

Zechariah — touching them touches His eye.

Comfort — electing protection under God’s wings.

Usage

"He kept him as the apple of his eye in the wilderness."

"Keep me as the apple of the eye, under the shadow of thy wings."

"He that toucheth you toucheth the apple of His eye."
